segments.text: Robinhood's Stock Tokens, stocks on a blockchain, trade around the clock.
But the stock price exists only six and a half hours a day.
Trades happen against a pool of tokens.
Liquidity providers fill it, and earn a fee per trade.
Their danger: a trader who knows the price just moved.
We replayed five point one million real trades.
While the market is open, a provider earns about a dollar per dollar lost.
segments.cap: While the market is open, a provider earns about $1 per $1 lost.

segments.text: At night, up to three. On weekends, three point eight to nineteen point five.
segments.cap: At night, up to $3. On weekends, $3.8 to $19.5.

segments.text: Pools differ by fee tier, and holders cannot see which pays.
Picking a pool by hand is guesswork.
Hooks, small programs inside pools, can keep a hidden cut. Eighty percent are flagged malicious.
segments.cap: Hooks, small programs inside pools, can keep a hidden cut. 80% are flagged malicious.

segments.text: It replays every pool and fee tier of each token, and picks where liquidity pays.
It only enters pools with no hidden cut, or a maximum fee the pool enforces.
We sent two hundred trades over the maximum, on a copy of the real chain.
segments.cap: We sent 200 trades over the maximum, on a copy of the real chain.

segments.text: For a holder, it is one deposit into a vault.
Deposit NVDA, and the vault earns the fees for you.
Uptick. Stock Token yield, chosen by the chain's own data.
